text.p: Buffton Corp said Monday it named Alan Tremain, O.B.E., as chairman, and Jean-Claude Mathot as president and chief operating officer.

Their appointments were announced by Robert McLean, chief executive officer of Buffton, who said the company has acquired from Tremain and Mathot all of the outstanding stock of Hotels of Distinction, Inc, in exchange for 300,000 common shares of Buffton.
McLean previously held the positions of chairman, president, chief operating officer and CEO. He will continue as CEO, the company said.
Hotels of Distinction is a Palm Beach, Fla.,-based hotel management firm founded by Tremain in 1974.
It manages hotels in the U.S., Canada and the Caribbean including the Copley Plaza Hotel in Boston, the Le Grand in Montreal, the Back Bay Hilton in Boston and the Cotton Bay Club in the Bahamas.

At Buffton, Hotels of Distinction will operate as a subsidiary of BFX Hospitality Group Inc. It will focus on the purchase and management of hotel properties in attractive secondary markets of the U.S.

BFX Hospitality owns and operates food service, lodging and entertainment companies in Texas and Louisiana. They include "Cabo, The Original 'Mix Mex' Grill," in Houston, the Stockyards Hotel and Lucile's Restaurant, both in Ft. Worth, and the Cat's Meow in New Orleans.

Tremain is a director of Florida International University School of Hospitality Management and a director of the China Fund, Inc., a closed end fund invested in China and listed on the New York Stock Exchange.

In March 1988, he was bestowed the Order of the British Empire by the Queen of England, for his contribution to British-American commerce and for his leadership in the international hospitality industry.
Mathot served as executive vice president of Hotels of Distinction from 1974-1992 and has been its president and chief operating officer since 1992.

Buffton is a diversified group of companies with operations in the hospitality and electrical products industries. Buffton previously announced its plans to divest Current Technology Inc., its electric filter and power conversion company, to Danaher Corp.
